rows.title: StatCan reports manufacturing sales essentially unchanged in September
rows.summary: Statistics Canada reported that Canadian manufacturing sales were essentially flat in September at about $80.2 billion, with sales down in 11 of 21 subsectors, led by primary metals (-9.5%) and wood products (-7.0%). Petroleum and coal product sales jumped 10.0%, mainly because of higher prices rather than more output. Once price changes are removed (constant dollars), manufacturing sales actually fell 1.5%, meaning factories shipped less product even though the dollar total held steady. A separate StatCan report showed wholesale sales excluding petroleum and grain rose 0.7% to $92.5 billion but also fell 0.2% in volume terms. The figures add to signs that real growth in Canada was weak at the end of the third quarter, as factories face steep U.S. tariffs.
rows.fact: September manufacturing sales were roughly unchanged at $80.2 billion but fell 1.5% in constant dollars; primary metals dropped 9.5% and wood products 7.0%, while petroleum and coal rose 10.0% on higher prices. Wholesale sales excluding petroleum and grain rose 0.7% to $92.5 billion but slipped 0.2% in volume.
rows.why: 공장 매출 '금액'은 그대로인데 가격 효과를 빼면 실제 생산량은 1.5% 줄었다는 점에서, 명목 지표와 실질 지표의 차이로 경제의 실제 체력을 읽는 법을 배울 수 있기 때문입니다.
rows.why_en: Factory sales held steady in dollars but shrank 1.5% once price effects are removed, which teaches how the gap between nominal and real figures reveals an economy's true strength.
rows.term_def: A way of measuring sales after removing the effect of price changes, so you can see whether the actual quantity of goods sold went up or down, not just whether prices rose.
rows.note: 7-day fallback (no federal or Bank of Canada policy action in the last 24h). StatCan manufacturing and wholesale releases of Nov 13 (8:30 ET); CP body read in full and cross-checked against the identical CP text on Advisor.ca.

opinion.title: Industry data point to tepid Canadian growth in late Q3
opinion.author: Claire Fan, Annie Zheng
opinion.summary: Written as a preview of the September manufacturing and wholesale reports, the note argues the data would confirm that Canada grew more slowly in the third quarter than forecast. With July and August GDP flat and StatCan's flash estimate pointing to a small September contraction, the economists put Q3 annualized growth near 1.3%, below RBC's and the Bank of Canada's earlier estimates. They stress that a small nominal rise in factory sales hid a much larger drop in volume, because manufacturing prices, especially refinery prices, rose sharply and U.S. auto plant stoppages hit cross-border trade. Firmer wholesale sales, they say, would only partly offset the weakness.
opinion.why: 은행 이코노미스트들이 물가 상승분을 걷어내 '진짜 생산량'을 계산하고 이를 GDP 전망으로 연결하는 과정을 보여주어, 경제 지표 분석이 실제로 어떻게 이루어지는지 배울 수 있기 때문입니다.
opinion.why_en: It shows how bank economists strip out price increases to estimate real output and link it to GDP forecasts, a hands-on look at how economic data is actually analyzed.

rows.title: US starts 2027 fiscal year with record October budget deficit of $404 billion
rows.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department reported a $404 billion budget deficit for October, the first month of fiscal 2027, a record for the month and 42% more than a year earlier. Spending hit a record $773 billion, up 12%, driven by farm relief payments, higher military spending and $115 billion in gross interest on the federal debt, while receipts fell 9% to $369 billion. Net customs (tariff) collections dropped 39% to $19.2 billion from their peak a year earlier. Part of the gap reflects timing, since some November benefit payments were shifted into October, but even after adjusting for that the deficit was $285 billion, up 49%. Fiscal 2026 ended with a deficit of nearly $2 trillion, or 6.2% of GDP, far above Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's 3% goal.
rows.fact: Treasury data show a record October deficit of $404 billion ($285 billion after calendar adjustment), with outlays at a record $773 billion and receipts down 9% to $369 billion. Customs receipts fell 39% to $19.2 billion, while interest costs on the debt rose to $115 billion.
rows.why: 정부가 세금보다 더 많이 쓰면 빚을 내야 하고, 늘어나는 이자 비용과 줄어드는 관세 수입이 미국 재정에 어떤 영향을 주는지 실제 숫자로 이해할 수 있기 때문입니다.
rows.why_en: When a government spends more than it collects it must borrow, and this story uses real numbers to show how rising interest costs and shrinking tariff revenue affect U.S. public finances.
rows.term_def: The amount by which government spending exceeds its revenue (taxes, tariffs and so on) in a period; the government covers the gap by borrowing, mostly by selling Treasury bonds, which adds to the national debt.
rows.note: 7-day fallback (weekend; no new U.S. policy action in the last 24h). Official Monthly Treasury Statement released Nov 12 ET; Reuters body read in full and figures cross-checked with American Action Forum's analysis of the same statement.

opinion.title: Debt and Deficit (Lack of) Progress Report: October 2026
opinion.author: Jordan Haring
opinion.summary: Haring, fiscal policy director at the center-right American Action Forum, walks through the October Treasury statement and finds revenue down $35 billion, mostly from lower individual income taxes and a 39% fall in customs duties. He links the customs drop to tariff changes made by executive action and to refunds after the Supreme Court ruled the IEEPA tariffs illegal. Spending rose $84 billion, led by defense, Medicare and Social Security, and interest payments climbed because the debt is larger and long-term rates are higher. With debt held by the public at $32.7 trillion, nearly double its October 2019 level, he argues the U.S. fiscal path is unsustainable.
opinion.why: 관세 수입 감소, 사회보장 지출, 이자 부담이 어떻게 합쳐져 국가부채를 키우는지 정리해 주어 '재정 지속가능성' 개념을 이해하는 데 도움이 되기 때문입니다.
opinion.why_en: It explains how falling tariff revenue, entitlement spending and rising interest costs together push up the national debt, helping readers understand fiscal sustainability.

rows.title: ICT exports log record-high growth in Oct. amid AI boom
rows.summary: South Korea's exports of information and communications technology (ICT) goods reached $70.35 billion in October, about triple the $23.29 billion of a year earlier, according to Ministry of Science and ICT data released on Sunday. That was the fastest growth rate on record and the second-largest monthly total after September. Semiconductors drove the jump: chip exports rose 259.4% to $56.47 billion on strong demand for premium memory and high memory prices, and computer and accessory exports grew more than fivefold on demand for server SSDs. ICT products made up about 61% of Korea's total exports, staying above 60% for a third straight month. ICT exports to China tripled and exports to the U.S. grew more than sixfold, showing how closely Korea's trade now tracks the global AI investment cycle.
rows.fact: October ICT exports were $70.35 billion, up about 202% on-year, with chips at $56.47 billion (+259.4%) and mobile phones up 6.5%. ICT goods accounted for about 61% of all Korean exports in the month.
rows.why: AI 투자 붐이 메모리 가격과 수출액을 폭발적으로 끌어올리는 모습을 통해, 한 나라의 무역이 특정 산업과 세계 경기 사이클에 얼마나 크게 의존할 수 있는지 이해할 수 있기 때문입니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how an AI investment boom can send memory prices and export values soaring, and how heavily one country's trade can come to depend on a single industry and the global cycle.
rows.term_def: How much of a country's exports come from just one product or industry; high concentration means big gains in a boom but big risks if that industry's prices fall.
rows.note: Last-24h official data release (Ministry of Science and ICT, Sun Nov 15 KST). Yonhap body read; headline figures cross-checked with Seoul Economic Daily (Nov 15).

opinion.title: AI chip boom jump-starts Taiwan's consumer spending, but not Korea's
opinion.author: Kim Won
opinion.summary: Drawing on a Bank of Korea research report, the piece explains why the AI chip boom is spreading into household spending in Taiwan but not in Korea: Taiwan's private consumption grew 5.4% in the first three quarters of 2026, against 2.1% in Korea. Part of the gap is jobs, since IT manufacturing employs about 10.6% of Taiwan's workforce but only 1.9% of Korea's. Korea's chip export values are rising mainly because prices are up rather than volumes, so they lift export figures without a matching rise in production and hiring. The BOK warns domestic demand may recover only slowly unless the gains spread to other industries and middle- and lower-income households.
opinion.why: 수출 '숫자'가 좋아도 일자리와 가계 소비로 이어지지 않으면 경제 전체가 나아지지 않는다는 'K자형 양극화'의 원리를 대만과의 비교로 쉽게 보여주기 때문입니다.
opinion.why_en: By comparing Korea with Taiwan, it explains the K-shaped divide: strong export numbers do not lift the whole economy unless they turn into jobs and household spending.

rows.title: Germany set for near-record new borrowing in 2027 after difficult budget deal
rows.summary: In the early hours of Friday, Nov 13, the German parliament's budget committee agreed a 2027 federal budget with €561 billion in spending and more than €210 billion in total new borrowing, just below the 2021 pandemic record of €215.4 billion. About €123 billion of the borrowing comes from the core budget, on top of extra debt allowed under special funds for defence and infrastructure. To reach the deal, Chancellor Friedrich Merz's coalition dropped a plastic packaging tax, delayed a sugary-drinks tax to 2028 and reversed welfare cuts for children of low-income families. A planned electricity-tax cut was postponed because the committee could not agree on €5 billion to pay for it. The budget now goes to a full parliamentary vote, while Germany's Council of Economic Experts expects only about 1% growth next year.
rows.fact: The Bundestag budget committee cleared the 2027 budget with €561 billion in spending and about €210 billion in total new borrowing, roughly €123 billion of it in the core budget. Several revenue and savings measures were dropped or delayed, and the electricity-tax cut Merz championed was postponed.
rows.outlook: Berenberg's Holger Schmieding called the budget less ambitious than economically desirable, and Merz expects coalition talks on the electricity-tax cut to continue.
rows.why: 유럽 최대 경제국 독일이 국방·인프라 투자를 위해 사상 두 번째 규모의 빚을 내기로 한 결정은, 적자 재정으로 성장을 떠받치는 것과 미래 세대의 이자 부담 사이의 균형을 이해하는 좋은 사례이기 때문입니다.
rows.why_en: Germany, Europe's largest economy, is borrowing at its second-highest level on record to fund defence and infrastructure, a good case for understanding the trade-off between deficit-financed growth and future interest burdens.
rows.term_def: The extra money a government borrows in a year because its spending is higher than its tax and other income; it adds to total public debt, which must later be repaid with interest.
rows.note: 7-day fallback (no European policy announcement in the last 24h). Budget committee deal of Nov 13 (Berlin); Reuters body read in full and figures cross-checked with dpa and the federal government's budget page. Different event from the Nov 11 expert council report.

opinion.title: Economists warn of severe budget crisis in Germany starting in 2028
opinion.author: dpa (with Clemens Fuest, Achim Wambach, Jens Boysen-Hogrefe)
opinion.summary: Leading German economists, reacting to the 2027 budget, argue Berlin's fiscal course cannot last and that a serious budget crisis looms from 2028. ifo president Clemens Fuest says other spending should be frozen or cut while defence and infrastructure take priority, or tax increases will become unavoidable. ZEW president Achim Wambach warns that with interest rates above growth, the state cannot grow its way out of debt, so welfare reform and cuts to non-growth subsidies should come first. The Kiel Institute and the head of the federal audit court add that an ageing population and a rising interest bill mean Germany is living beyond its means.
opinion.why: 금리가 성장률보다 높으면 정부가 성장만으로 빚을 줄일 수 없다는 핵심 재정 원리를 실제 독일 사례로 보여주기 때문입니다.
opinion.why_en: It uses Germany's real situation to show a key principle of public finance: when interest rates exceed growth, a government cannot simply grow its way out of debt.

rows.title: Only 28% of PLI employment target met by FY26, says NITI Aayog report
rows.summary: NITI Aayog, the Indian government's policy think tank, released its first full assessment of the 14 Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes, which pay companies subsidies tied to extra output in sectors such as electronics, pharmaceuticals and autos. By FY26 the schemes had created about 849,000 jobs against a target of 3 million (about 28%), while investment reached Rs 2.4 trillion (76% of target) and production Rs 22.66 trillion (64%). The report says jobs lag because companies invest first, ramp up output next, and hire only once they reach commercial scale. Electronics, pharmaceutical drugs, telecom equipment and food products were judged on track, while medical-device jobs, bulk-drug exports and IT-hardware investment were weak. It urges a shift from uniform supply-side subsidies toward sector-specific design plus demand-side support such as government procurement and export promotion.
rows.fact: The 14 PLI schemes launched in 2020-21 met about 28% of their employment target by FY26, but 76% of their investment target and 64% of their production target. Job creation fell from well above the annual target in 2024-25 to 31% of it in 2025-26.
rows.outlook: NITI Aayog says it is too early to judge the schemes against full-tenure targets, and schemes needing changes will be reviewed with the relevant ministries.
rows.why: 정부 보조금이 공장 투자와 생산은 크게 늘렸지만 일자리는 목표의 28%에 그친 인도의 사례는, 산업정책의 효과와 한계를 이해하는 데 좋은 교재가 되기 때문입니다.
rows.why_en: India's case, where subsidies boosted factory investment and output but delivered only 28% of the promised jobs, is a good lesson in what industrial policy can and cannot do.
rows.term_def: A government subsidy paid to companies only after they actually produce or sell more than a set baseline, used to attract factories into chosen industries.
rows.note: 7-day fallback (Japan Q3 GDP and China October activity data are due Nov 16, not yet out). NITI Aayog report released Nov 12 IST; Business Standard body read in full and cross-checked with the government's PIB press release.

opinion.title: NITI Aayog–IIM Ahmedabad Report on PLI: Manufacturing gains; Jobs, tech growth & self-reliance is the next big push
opinion.author: Vivek Kumar
opinion.summary: The piece argues that PLI has succeeded at building factories at scale, but its real test now is whether those factories create jobs and domestic technology. It points to the 28% jobs figure and to battery-cell capacity far below its goal, explaining the gaps with the report's findings: hiring lags investment, automation, assembly outpacing component making, rigid early scheme rules and barriers for small firms. It closes on a positive note, presenting the report's reform agenda and newer component schemes as signs that policy is correcting itself. The outlet is a weekly close to the ruling party's ideological camp, and its tone is favorable to the government.
opinion.why: 공장을 짓는 것과 일자리·기술을 만드는 것이 왜 다른 문제인지, 그리고 산업정책이 시행착오를 거쳐 어떻게 수정되는지를 보여주기 때문입니다.
opinion.why_en: It shows why building factories is not the same as creating jobs and technology, and how industrial policy gets revised through trial and error.
